cells.tense: The pattern sits in front of you now, and you are reading what it means.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: When the pattern lands and you know what it means, gather the feelings it might bring and hold them loosely for a day before choosing one to move from.
cells.core:
You cut through the thing that wasn't true, and it came down without being pushed. What you saw was a structure standing on a false premise, and once you said it plainly, it gave way — not a crash, a clearing. You stand on the open ground that follows and read the shape of the room as it actually is, and the reading does its work without forcing.

Before you leave this ground, gather what you might feel about what you saw. All the possible feelings — relief, maybe, some grief for time the structure took, something not yet named — and hold them together without choosing one to be the true one yet. From the whole cloud comes a felt recognition that honours what you saw and doesn't fuse itself to it.
cells.sheetLine: The false structure fell. The ground under it is clear.
cells.verb: cutting through the false structure with a logic that doesn't wait
cells.place: on the sudden ground where what couldn't hold has come down

cells.tense: You are bracing for the next false structure before this clearing has finished.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: Whatever the clearing showed you needs settling, settle it now and see it through today, owing nobody your reasons.
cells.core:
A pattern got cut through and the ground opened, and now the future is being built over the open place before anyone has walked there. Every next move is decided in advance, and each decision arrives with its reasons already stapled on — spoken, defended, made impossible to be wrong about. The clearing was sudden. The filling of it is being enforced. What cuts sharply used to wait to arrive; lately it settles first and arrives after.

Go on and do the thing the open ground is asking for. Settle what needs settling, then see it done before the day turns, and hand nobody your reasoning. The call can carry itself. Judgement of this kind doesn't need the proof, and the proof is what has been eating the ground.
cells.sheetLine: You're paving the clearing before the dust has settled.

cells.tense: You were standing in front of the false structure, and the collapse happened behind your back.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Name the tie or habit the old structure stood on, then take one step toward the people it actually connects you to.
cells.core:
The structure came down, and you didn't walk into the clearing it left. You stayed at the edge, where the old lines are still faintly visible on the ground. What you see is sharp enough, and none of it has been spent on where you are now. The people the structure held have moved into the open. You are still at the rim of where it used to stand.

There is a connection the false thing was standing in for — a real tie underneath the arrangement. Walk toward it. Leave the habit or the routine that kept the old shape up, and take one step toward the person or group the real thing lives in. Going deeper than what was comfortable is the whole crossing. What connects lies on the other side of the leaving.

cells.tense: The clearing is happening and the person who made the cut is not claiming it.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Follow a pull you haven't named — toward a person, a place, a piece of work — and go look at it close up, just to find out what it is.
cells.core:
A false structure came down, and in your account it fell by itself. You were the one who saw the pattern that brought it down. You did the cutting. Asked, your answer is that you merely spotted something. But the spotting was the act, and the open ground you stand on is yours to claim. You talk as if you walked into a room already empty.

The pull you feel toward what might come next is the earlier form of the same line. Follow it a little way. Go toward the thing that draws you — a person, a place, a piece of work — and look at it close up, once, just to find out what it actually is. Before you were seeing patterns to break them, you were drawn to look. Go, and the ground you cleared has something in it, and you are the one who went.

attempts.check: The record does not support reading the person's exact history — something in a draft wants to say the false structure was built by the person or cost years; the record only names the mechanism and the seat. The reader could reasonably say the structure cleared, or is clearing, from outside — that the collapse wasn't their recognition at all. The asks survive being wrong: each is small, doable, and teaches something even if the read is off. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line admiring the speed of the cut; I've cut those and kept the plain thing.
